result.title: Game-Guided Skill Discovery through Self-Play for Playable Agent Control
result.summary: We present Game-Guided Skill Discovery (GGSD), a framework that uses self-play in games to discover motor skills that are directly playable by humans. Playable skills provide a compact abstraction for controlling embodied agents through a small set of learned behaviors rather than low-level actions. To be effective, these skills should be semantically distinct, interpretable, and expressive; properties that existing unsupervised skill-discovery methods often fail to achieve simultaneously. GGSD achieves these desiderata by grounding skill discovery in competitive gameplay. A hierarchical agent competes against its past selves, with a high-level policy selecting from a small discrete skill set and a skill-conditioned low-level policy learning the corresponding behaviors. After training, a human can replace the high-level policy and directly control the agent through the same discrete skills. Despite the small number of high-level actions, skill transitions give rise to emergent combo behaviors, expanding expressivity beyond individual primitives. Across Ant, Franka-arm, and Unitree G1 environments, we show that GGSD produces human-playable skills that humans can compose to solve unseen tasks, such as Maze and CubePush, without additional training. An interactive demo is available at https://ggsd-demo.github.io.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GGSD 框架，通过在游戏中自博弈发现可由人类直接操作的运动技能：高层策略从少量离散技能中选取，低层策略学习对应行为，技能切换产生涌现的组合行为，并在多个具身环境中验证人类可用这些技能解决未见过任务。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作把控制抽象为小规模离散技能集并研究技能切换带来的组合表达力，与 LVR 中「离散 latent 状态/推理步骤的选择与组合能否扩展表达力」的问题可能相关，可作为一个概念性对照线索核查，但对象是运动控制而非视觉语言推理。
